style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, 90-degree top-down, of a supplier deduction statement on a brushed-steel receiving desk in a loading bay office. The bone-white fee-schedule sheet lies off-centre on the right third, fanned across a printed purchase-order form and an advance-ship-notice printout, one lower sheet pulled askew as if handled, faint illegible print, a red ballpoint pen resting across a circled line item, generous bare brushed steel at the left. Even diffused daylight from the left through a high window, soft graphite shadows pooling at the sheet edges, oxidised-red annotation marks the only colour, polymer clipboard clipped at the frame edge, 50mm, fine film grain, no legible text, no people, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, legible words, legible numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story's protagonist is a printed artefact of price and policy — a fee schedule on a deduction statement sitting on top of purchase orders and ship notices — which is exactly the regulatory/contractual territory the document still life was built for. A top-down flat-lay makes the three-class arithmetic legible as three distinct sheets with the cheap, red-circled data-defect page on top, and it rotates the desk onto its only never-used treatment.
cue: three separate cost curves wearing one deduction statement
subject: a supplier's printed deduction statement fanned over purchase-order and advance-ship-notice forms on a brushed-steel receiving desk
core_thesis: Walmart's supplier fine schedule is three fee classes, not one 3% number — and the cheapest class, billed $200 per data defect a supplier can fix in-house, makes the arithmetic itself pick the first spend.
core_conflict: Cheap in-house data hygiene (EDI, ASN, master data) that can retire the $200-per-defect class versus the expensive fill-rate class that only real safety-stock money can close — while ops leaders keep budgeting 'the Walmart fine' as one line.
composition: Top-down 90-degree flat-lay, hero deduction statement off-centre on the right third, secondary sheets fanned beneath with one pulled askew, a red pen crossing the frame diagonally, generous bare desk at the left
